items.title: 프라다가 열고 뎀나의 구찌가 잇는다… 역대 최대 규모 밀라노 패션위크 온다
items.summary: WWD Korea previews the September 2026 Milan Fashion Week calendar (largest edition yet, ~218 events, ~141,000 visitors), flagging Demna's Gucci presentation on September 25 at 2pm as one of the week's most-anticipated moments, following Prada's September 22 opening show. Frames the Gucci slot as a key marker for the 2027 spring/summer season narrative.

items.title: Demna's Gucci Back Under the Microscope at Milan Fashion Week
items.summary: BoF's week-ahead briefing frames Demna's September 25 show as his second (some count third) outing for Gucci, a year after his debut, positioning it as a test of whether his creative reset is working. Notes Gucci sits at the center of Kering's recovery math and that accessory design choices (clasp logic, strap architecture, leather treatment) will be watched closely as they tend to set the bag conversation for the year; a skeptical, results-oriented framing rather than promotional coverage.

items.title: 古驰大地震：换帅降价关百家店，这3个变化你必须看懂
items.summary: Weibo FAQ-style post summarizing Gucci's simultaneous shocks for Chinese consumers this month: new creative leadership under Demna, price cuts of up to 30-40% on core bag lines, and roughly 100 store closures in China (about 30% of the domestic fleet) since the start of the year. Comment threads reflect mixed sentiment: some users welcome the narrower price gap with overseas markets, others read the closures as confirmation the brand has lost premium status domestically.

items.title: 古驰的调价策略会对其在中国市场的销售产生什么影响？
items.summary: Weibo discussion thread on whether Gucci's official China price cuts will lift sales, citing store traffic reportedly up over 20% post-cut and some discounted styles selling out in the 2,000-5,000 yuan range. Commenters debate whether repeat discounting trains shoppers to wait for markdowns rather than restoring brand desirability, a recurring skeptical thread in the replies.

items.title: 구찌 실적 관련 커뮤니티 반응 스레드
items.summary: Korean community board thread reacting to coverage of Gucci's continued sales decline and China price cuts, with commenters debating whether repeated past price hikes permanently damaged the brand's desirability versus competitors like Chanel and Hermes; several posts express skepticism that Demna's design direction alone can reverse the trend.

items.title: グッチ アイウェア 2026年秋冬コレクションの新キャンペーンを発表
items.summary: Kering Japan press release announcing Gucci's FW2026 eyewear campaign, featuring portrait photography of subjects in reflective, individual moments. Highlights include black acetate Double-G optical frames and round sunglasses with Horsebit temple details, men's rectangular acetate frames, and round metal opticals with crossed Horsebit motifs. Standard official activation coverage.

items.source: Udedokei Toushi (腕時計投資.com resale market data)
items.title: グッチ価格相場・推移
items.summary: Japanese secondhand/resale market tracker shows Gucci's overall resale price index trending downward over the past six months, with the sharpest single drop of -26.5% recorded in early June. Notes that core lines (GG Marmont, Ophidia, Horsebit 1955) remain comparatively stable even as the broader resale trend is down, offering a community-sourced counterpoint to official brand messaging.

items.title: 「グッチ」がメンズ向けスモールレザーグッズを発売 日本限定ウオレットも
items.summary: WWD Japan reports Gucci's launch of a men's small leather goods line in Japan, including a Japan-exclusive wallet. Positioned as part of the brand's push to rebuild core-category volume (accessories/leather goods) alongside the broader Demna-era repositioning; straightforward trade coverage, non-critical.

items.title: 구찌 관련 개인 스레드 게시물
items.summary: Korean Threads post from a fashion-interested account discussing Gucci's recent business news (price cuts, store closures) and Demna's design direction, mixing personal opinion with reposted news commentary; engagement figures not visible on the fetched page.

items.title: 구찌, 2026 가을·겨울 아이웨어 새 시선
items.summary: Korean lifestyle-media writeup of the same FW2026 eyewear campaign (art direction Ricardo Zanola, photography Mark Seliger), emphasizing the Double-G and Horsebit design codes on updated silhouettes. Standard activation coverage, no critical angle; included for NEA-region distribution breadth beyond the Japan press-release version.
